text:
eli: euc2 GPU pool spike at ~11:01 UTC, scale-up requests were emitted but new nodes never became Ready. lots of Pending pods with `0/1` GPU capacity errors. noticed autoscaler kept bouncing between 2 scale attempts then cancelling
maya: same, dashboard shows surge at 11:01-11:03 and the provisioner reported successful create but kube didn't mark nodes Ready. looks like kubelet never joined, maybe CNI timing out :thinking_face:
sam: digging into provisioner logs. seeing a pattern: provisioner created instances -> cloud reports instance running -> kubelet heartbeat doesn't land within gracePeriod window -> node controller treats as NotReady -> autoscaler treats as failed and retriggers, which starts another create -> we end up with overlaps and throttle
priyanka: can you paste the error lines? also what was gracePeriod? last rollout changed it to 60s for faster teardown
sam: logs
```
2026-03-15T11:01:07Z provisioner: instance i-0a1b2c3d created in eu-central-2
2026-03-15T11:01:42Z cloud: instance i-0a1b2c3d RUNNING
2026-03-15T11:02:10Z kubelet(i-0a1b2c3d): failed to start CNI plugin: timed out after 120s
2026-03-15T11:02:30Z node-controller: node i-0a1b2c3d Registered but NotReady
2026-03-15T11:02:35Z autoscaler: scale attempt canceled (node NotReady) -> retrying
```
maya: CNI timed out for 120s, but gracePeriod=60s earlier - that mismatch will cause the node to be cut before CNI finishes
alejandro: this explains thrash. autoscaler sees no capacity and kicks again -> more instances -> increased cost and API request storms to cloud provider
priyanka: immediate mitigation: 1) increase node gracePeriod to 300s in nodepool config, 2) temporarily disable autoscaler aggressive retry (set backoff to 180s), 3) add a short circuit to route new traffic to eu-west1 fallback pool
eli: on it. patching nodepool and autoscaler now. @oncall /ops-bot can we kick traffic shift to eu-west1 for the next 10m?
oncall: ack, triggering route-shift, will gradually move 20% -> 100% over 5m
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0357 created: "eus2 provisioner heartbeat mismatch causing autoscaler thrash" assigned to infra-oncall
sam: after increasing gracePeriod I see nodes stabilize, CNI finishes, kubelet heartbeats appear and Pending pods start binding
priyanka: keep autoscaler backoff increased for 30m, we'll monitor token usage and cloud API quotas, and revert once stable
alejandro: cost note: this thrash generated ~15 extra node creations in 5m; estimate ~0.6k USD spike for region during incident. put on bill-watch
maya: logging action items: 1) align CNI timeout and node gracePeriod (prefer larger), 2) add gating so provisioner marks node Ready only after kubelet heartbeat + CNI success, 3) autoscaler should ignore transient NotReady for X seconds if instance creation timestamp < Y (creation age threshold), 4) add circuit breaker to stop retries when provider rate-limit errors seen
eli: will open follow-ups in infra backlog and tag owners. immediate postmortem to include timeline and a quant of cost impact
infra-bot: follow-up created: INFRA-1429 (align gracePeriod & CNI), INFRA-1430 (autoscaler backoff tuning), INFRA-1431 (provisioner readiness gate)
priyanka: nice work team, monitoring looks good now, reducing traffic shift back in 10m if no regression :thumbsup:
